subject.title: Exploring a chat-first Android surface for OpenClaw (discussion + possible focused upstreaming)

question: Should the official Android app adopt a chat-first default or mode, accept only focused UX/media PR slices while keeping the current Overview/Connect-first companion-node flow, or leave chat-first Android forks external for now?
rationale: Current main has substantial Android chat improvements, but changing the default surface or accepting broader fork media/navigation slices affects onboarding, pairing, permissions, release posture, and Android product direction.

options.title: Scope focused Android PR slices
options.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity slices that need real-device or emulator proof before PR acceptance.

options.title: Keep current companion-node flow
options.body: State that the official app remains Overview/Connect-first and invite only specific defects or small polish PRs against that model.

options.title: Sponsor chat-first mode
options.body: Explicitly sponsor a chat-first default or mode and require onboarding, upgrade, media-permission, and release proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Scope focused Android PR slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity slices that need real-device or emulator proof before PR acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is Android app product scope, and @obviyus is the named Android maintainer with relevant chat, assistant launch, and mobile connectivity history.
